categories.name: Storytelling and imagination
categories.tip: For personal and imaginative topics: open with a picture, add a turn, and end with what you learnt.

phrases.text: Close your eyes and picture…
phrases.example: Close your eyes and picture a city where the buses fly.

phrases.text: It all began on an ordinary morning.
phrases.example: It all began on an ordinary morning, when the clock refused to tick.

phrases.text: And then, without warning, everything changed.
phrases.example: And then, without warning, everything changed: the lights went out.

phrases.text: If I could…, I would…
phrases.example: If I could pause time, I would spend that hour with my grandparents.

phrases.text: Years from now, I hope to look back and say…
phrases.example: Years from now, I hope to look back and say that I stayed curious.

phrases.text: What surprised me most was…
phrases.example: What surprised me most was how quiet the world became.

phrases.text: The lesson I carry with me is…
phrases.example: The lesson I carry with me is that courage begins with a small step.

phrases.text: Maybe the real question is not what we lose, but what we notice.
phrases.example: Maybe the real question is not what we lose, but what we notice when it is gone.

categories.name: Openings & hooks
categories.tip: Your first 15 seconds decide whether they listen. Start with a hook, then state your stance.

phrases.text: Imagine a classroom where every child, not just the lucky few, has a seat.
phrases.example: Imagine a classroom where every child, not just the lucky few, has a seat. That is what fair education means.

phrases.text: Let me begin with a question that deserves an honest answer:
phrases.example: Let me begin with a question that deserves an honest answer: do we really listen to our elders?

phrases.text: There is a number that should keep every one of us awake at night.
phrases.note: Fact hook: follow with a statistic
phrases.example: There is a number that should keep every one of us awake at night: seven million tonnes of plastic enter our oceans every year.

phrases.text: Some say it is a problem; I say it is an opportunity wearing a disguise.
phrases.example: Some say pollution is a problem; I say it is an opportunity wearing a disguise, a chance to build cleaner cities.

phrases.text: A wise person once said, and I could not agree more:
phrases.example: A wise person once said, and I could not agree more: "Be the change you wish to see in the world."

phrases.text: Ladies and gentlemen, today I want to take you on a three-minute journey.
phrases.example: Ladies and gentlemen, today I want to take you on a three-minute journey into the world of social media.

phrases.text: Picture this: it is 2050 and the world looks very different.
phrases.example: Picture this: it is 2050 and the world looks very different. Every home runs on sunlight.

phrases.text: If you remember only one thing from this speech, let it be this:
phrases.example: If you remember only one thing from this speech, let it be this: kindness costs nothing but changes everything.

categories.name: Stating your stance
categories.tip: Say where you stand in one clear sentence, then preview your points.

phrases.text: I firmly believe that…
phrases.example: I firmly believe that homework should be balanced with play, because children need both to grow.

phrases.text: My position is simple: …, and I will prove it in three ways.
phrases.example: My position is simple: sport belongs in every school, and I will prove it in three ways.

phrases.text: While there are two sides to this, I stand firmly on the side of…
phrases.example: While there are two sides to this, I stand firmly on the side of protecting forests.

phrases.text: The answer, in my view, is not a matter of 'if' but of 'how'.
phrases.example: The answer, in my view, is not a matter of 'if' but of 'how': we must teach children digital safety.

phrases.text: Today I will argue that… for three reasons: …, …, and ….
phrases.example: Today I will argue that exams need reform for three reasons: stress, memory-only testing, and unfair pressure.

phrases.text: Let me be clear from the start: I am convinced that…
phrases.example: Let me be clear from the start: I am convinced that every girl deserves the same chances as every boy.

categories.name: Transitions
categories.tip: Signposts tell the audience where you are. Use one between every point.

phrases.text: Having looked at the problem, let us now turn to the solution.
phrases.example: Having looked at the problem of plastic waste, let us now turn to the solution: reuse and recycling.

phrases.text: That brings me to my second point.
phrases.example: We have seen why sleep matters. That brings me to my second point: how screens steal it.

phrases.text: But that is only one side of the coin.
phrases.example: Cheap fuel helps families today. But that is only one side of the coin: the air we breathe pays the price.

phrases.text: Building on this idea, consider…
phrases.example: Reading builds vocabulary. Building on this idea, consider how it also builds empathy.

phrases.text: Equally important is…
phrases.example: Fixing roads is good; equally important is making sure they are safe for walkers and cyclists.

phrases.text: This is where the story takes an interesting turn.
phrases.example: The village had no school for years. This is where the story takes an interesting turn: a teacher arrived.

phrases.text: Now, you may be wondering: what can we actually do?
phrases.example: We know the dangers of pollution. Now, you may be wondering: what can we actually do?

phrases.text: Let me illustrate this with an example.
phrases.example: Teamwork is easy to praise. Let me illustrate this with an example from our own cricket team.

categories.name: Introducing examples & evidence
categories.tip: A point without an example is only an opinion. Introduce evidence smoothly.

phrases.text: Take, for instance, the case of…
phrases.example: Take, for instance, the case of Indore, which became India's cleanest city by separating waste at home.

phrases.text: The evidence speaks for itself: …
phrases.example: The evidence speaks for itself: countries that educate girls grow richer and healthier.

phrases.text: Consider what happened in…
phrases.example: Consider what happened in Odisha, where early cyclone warnings saved thousands of lives.

phrases.text: According to… , nearly…
phrases.note: Always name a source if you can
phrases.example: According to the health ministry, nearly one in five teenagers feels constant stress.

phrases.text: A powerful illustration of this is…
phrases.example: A powerful illustration of this is the Chipko movement, where villagers hugged trees to save them.

phrases.text: History offers us a striking lesson: …
phrases.example: History offers us a striking lesson: societies that ignored public health paid dearly in epidemics.

phrases.text: Look no further than our own country: …
phrases.example: Look no further than our own country: UPI has made digital payments possible for a street vendor.

phrases.text: To put this in perspective, …
phrases.example: To put this in perspective, a single plastic bottle can outlive three generations of one family.

categories.name: Presenting both sides
categories.tip: Showing the other side makes you sound fair and wins trust before you argue your own.

phrases.text: On the one hand,… ; on the other hand,…
phrases.example: On the one hand, social media connects friends across the world; on the other hand, it can steal our sleep.

phrases.text: Critics argue that…, and they have a point. However,…
phrases.example: Critics argue that online classes are tiring, and they have a point. However, they reach children in remote villages.

phrases.text: It would be unfair to ignore the other side of the argument.
phrases.example: It would be unfair to ignore the other side of the argument: some people need the factory jobs.

phrases.text: There is no denying that…; yet we must also remember that…
phrases.example: There is no denying that technology makes life easy; yet we must also remember that it can make us lazy.

phrases.text: Supporters point to…, while opponents warn of…
phrases.example: Supporters point to cheaper power, while opponents warn of the risks of nuclear waste.

phrases.text: The truth, as is often the case, lies somewhere in between.
phrases.example: The truth, as is often the case, lies somewhere in between: use technology, but with limits.

categories.name: Rebuttals & counter-arguments
categories.tip: Disagree with ideas, never with people. Acknowledge, then redirect.

phrases.text: Some may say… but this overlooks a crucial fact.
phrases.example: Some may say recycling is too expensive, but this overlooks a crucial fact: waste costs far more.

phrases.text: That argument sounds convincing, but it does not hold up when we look closely.
phrases.example: That argument sounds convincing, but it does not hold up when we look closely at the numbers.

phrases.text: It is a common belief that…; the reality, however, is quite different.
phrases.example: It is a common belief that marks decide success; the reality, however, is quite different.

phrases.text: To those who claim…, I would ask: …?
phrases.example: To those who claim sport is a waste of time, I would ask: why do the best students also play?

phrases.text: I respect that view, but the numbers tell a different story.
phrases.example: I respect that view, but the numbers tell a different story: pollution is rising every year.

phrases.text: This is precisely where the argument falls short.
phrases.example: Saying small actions don't matter is precisely where the argument falls short; millions of small actions add up.

categories.name: Conclusions
categories.tip: End by signalling the close, recapping briefly, then leaving them with a memorable final line.

phrases.text: To conclude, …
phrases.example: To conclude, clean air is not a luxury; it is a right.

phrases.text: In a nutshell, …
phrases.example: In a nutshell, reading makes us wiser, kinder and braver.

phrases.text: So, the next time you…, remember that…
phrases.example: So, the next time you throw away a bottle, remember that the planet has no bin.

phrases.text: Let us not wait for tomorrow; the time to act is now.
phrases.example: Let us not wait for tomorrow; the time to act is now.

phrases.text: As we began with a question, let me end with an answer: …
phrases.example: As we began with a question, let me end with an answer: yes, every voice in a democracy counts.

phrases.text: The choice before us is clear, and the choice is ours.
phrases.example: The choice before us is clear, and the choice is ours.

phrases.text: If we do this, we do not merely solve a problem; we build a future.
phrases.example: If we protect our forests, we do not merely solve a problem; we build a future.

phrases.text: Thank you. Let us turn our words into action.
phrases.example: Thank you. Let us turn our words into action.

categories.name: Politics lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: The ballot is mightier than the bullet.
Accountability is the oxygen of democracy.
A government of the people must also be answerable to the people.
Silence in the face of injustice is a vote for the status quo.
Diplomacy is the art of making enemies think they are friends, and friends feel like family.
In international relations, there are no permanent friends or enemies, only permanent interests.

categories.name: Science & Tech lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: Technology is a tool; wisdom lies in how we use it.
We live in an age where information is abundant but attention is scarce.
Innovation begins where the comfort of the familiar ends.
Behind every algorithm is a human choice.
Science gives us the power; ethics must give us the direction.
The question is no longer what technology can do, but what it should do.

categories.name: Environment lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: There is no Planet B.
We do not inherit the earth from our ancestors; we borrow it from our children.
Sustainability is not a sacrifice; it is an investment.
The climate clock is ticking, and it is not waiting for us.
What we throw away does not disappear; it simply goes somewhere else.
Protecting nature is not charity; it is self-preservation.

categories.name: Society lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: A society is judged by how it treats its most vulnerable.
Education is the great equaliser.
Equality is not a gift to be given but a right to be claimed.
Progress is when tradition and change shake hands.
Every child is a promise; let us not break it.
Respect is the currency of a healthy society.

categories.name: Economy lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: Growth that does not reach the last person is not progress.
Inflation is the silent tax that hits the poorest hardest.
Employment is not just income; it is dignity.
A nation prospers when its young people have jobs and its jobs have purpose.
Entrepreneurs do not wait for opportunities; they build them.
India's demographic dividend can become a demographic disaster without skills and jobs.

categories.name: Education lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: Education is not the filling of a pail, but the lighting of a fire.
Marks measure memory; they do not measure potential.
We must teach students how to think, not what to think.
A classroom should be a place of curiosity, not of fear.
In the digital age, learning to learn is the most important skill.
Equal access to education is the foundation of every other equality.

categories.name: Media & Art lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: Freedom of the press is the heartbeat of democracy.
In an age of information overload, truth needs defenders.
Think before you share; a click can travel farther than a correction.
Art holds up a mirror to society and dares it to look.
When a language dies, a whole way of seeing the world dies with it.
With the power to influence comes the duty to inform.

categories.name: Healthcare lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: Health is wealth.
Prevention is better, and cheaper, than cure.
There is no health without mental health.
A strong nation begins with a healthy people.
Access to healthcare should never depend on the size of your wallet.
Technology can bridge the distance between a village and a specialist.

categories.name: Sports lines
categories.tip: Memorable lines to drop into a speech on this domain.

phrases.text: Sport teaches us how to lose with grace and win with humility.
Discipline is choosing what you want most over what you want now.
The finish line is just the beginning of a champion's character.
When a girl plays, a community changes.
Talent is universal, but opportunity is not.
In sport, as in life, it is not the fall that defines you, but how you rise.
